en: 9. The Question on the Crows’ Limbs “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two limbs of a crow are to be adopted,’ which are those two limbs that are to be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a crow moves about with suspicion and apprehension, being ever-watchful and diligent;”

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner who is devoted to yoga, being apprehensive and wary, should move about with mindfulness established and the sense faculties restrained through diligent effort.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the crow that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, whenever a crow sees any food, it shares it with its kinsmen before eating it.

In the same way, Great King, a yogin who is a practitioner of yoga should share with his virtuous fellow celibates whatever gains he has acquired in accordance with the Dhamma and righteously, even if it is merely the contents of his alms-bowl.
This, Great King, is the second quality to be adopted from the crow.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
“If ascetics bring me whatever they have obtained, ... [as found in the *Dhammapada* 386] ...”
"Having shared everything with all, I then eat my food.
The ninth question: The Question of the Flock of Crows.
